_about: Expected organic click-through rate by Google position, for measure rule MSR-004 (a target query at position <= 5 whose CTR is below ctrFloorRatio x the expected CTR). This is an INDUSTRY AVERAGE ESTIMATE from one published study, not this site's data: real CTR varies with query type, SERP features (AI Overview, local pack, snippets), brand queries and device. Use it as a yardstick, never as a forecast. positions[i] is the expected CTR at position i+1 (the shape scripts/measure.mjs reads).
label: industry average estimate (mixed queries and devices, SERPs with and without features)
source: Backlinko 'Google CTR Stats' (https://backlinko.com/google-ctr-stats), an industry-average estimate; position 1 confirmed 2026-10-22, positions 2-10 UNPROVEN (see study.verification)

study.name: Backlinko, 'Google CTR Stats' (Backlinko with Semrush data)
study.published: 2023 (the page's own date; confirm on the page)
study.verification: UNPROVEN beyond position 1. On 2026-10-22 a web-search snippet of the page confirmed: the #1 result has an average CTR of 27.6%; #1 is about 10x more likely to be clicked than #10; positions 8-10 are nearly equal with a bump at 8. The values for positions 2-10 below were NOT confirmed against the page in this build (the table is an image the search tool did not return); they are recalled and must be checked by opening the page before any report quotes them as the study's numbers.

beyond10.note: no study value: positions 11 and below use 1%; an authored placeholder, not a measurement
